svg.title: A limit with a ruler
svg.desc: Four parabolas with cubic intercepts trade total area for a larger smallest pocket. For span parameter epsilon between zero and one tenth, finite rational bounds enclose the first step until the two triangles tie. A left graph divides the actual cubic gain and sixth-order cost by their leading predictions; gold and blue bands enclose their correction factors. A right graph magnifies the ratio of cost to squared gain: it lies between one twelfth minus epsilon squared over twenty and one twelfth minus epsilon squared over twenty-five. All bands hold continuously. Central traces and decimals are rounded illustrations. At outer labels three and four, the minimum gains about 0.025216 percent for a total-area cost of about 0.0000005271 percent. Below, all three complete pockets at the first triangle tie have been straightened and rescaled by one common area-preserving change of coordinates. This certifies spans with endpoint ratio at most four thirds; the general positive-span frontier remains a separate question.

g.text: A tiny first improvement, now with finite error bounds.
Four curves. First grow the smaller triangle until both triangles tie.
How close are the leading laws?
Shaded bands are proved for every ε. The central traces are rounded illustrations.
Each percentage uses its own area at the largest-total placement as its baseline.
The complete two-stage frontier is proved on this span range. These errors concern its first step.
